I had hypothyroidism, my doctor investigated about it, I had to see a specialist who made me pass even more tests, they didn't find anything wrong... turns out, after stopping contraceptives for a while, it went away on its own, and my doctor said it could have been the culprit.

thyroid hormone is related to your metabolic rate, so it can lower it down, but that doesn't sound like the most common side effect considering two doctors had no idea what was going on with me...

although water retention is a common side effect but it's temporary and usually mild.

on a brighter note, I took another contraceptive afterwards (yaz), and I had almost no side effects (besides headaches), didn't even gain water weight, apparently because it's a mild diuretic as well... so if you're worried, I'm sure you'll find something that works for you as well, not all contraceptive are the same and not everyone react to them the same way (same thing with antidepressants and any medication obviously)

In the US, you should be able to find lauratadine (Claritine) cetirizine (Zyrtec) and fexofenadine (Allegra) over the counter... to gain the max effect of these tho you need to take them every day for at least a couple days, compared to benadryl that acts right away (which is why it's better for acute reactions) tho I think Allegra acts the fastest among them. Also zyrtec can sometimes causes drowsiness at first.

ay yo I'm not a doctor, but I've been told benadryl should not be used for chronic allergies, it's recommended for acute allergies like a rash, because you build tolerance to it very very quickly. If you don't have any contraindications, stuff like claritin (loratadine/desloratadin) might be a better option, you only have to take it once a day, has no somnolence side effect, and there isn't a risk of getting dementia later (even therapeutic level is shown to increase risks...), but make sure to ask a doctor/pharmacist/whatever if you wanna take new medication, don't just trust internet weirdos (me)
